item.title: TapeUp 0.1.5
item.description:
What's new

  • TapeUp remembers voices. Name a voice once, and TapeUp fills in that name the next time it hears the same person. A name TapeUp fills in is marked, so you can play the voice to check it or pick someone else. When you correct one, TapeUp shows earlier meetings where it made the same mistake, so you can check those too. Voices stay on your Mac.
  • Free up space. Choose Free Up Space… from the ··· menu to remove the audio from old recordings and keep their transcripts. It shows which recordings will lose their audio before you confirm. Lock any recording whose audio you want to keep. Recordings that still need a transcript or speaker labels keep their audio until those are done.
  • Rename someone everywhere. Rename a person on the People page, and the name changes in every recording. You can undo it.
  • Naming a voice adds that person to the meeting, and to your people list if they're new.
  • New commands for your agent. The command line can now import and transcribe a file, list and name voices, edit your people list, and remove or lock audio. Agents can lock audio but can't unlock it. To see the commands, run /Applications/TapeUp.app/Contents/MacOS/TapeUp help.

Install

Download TapeUp.dmg below and drag TapeUp to Applications, or:

brew install kkyrian/tap/tapeup

Already on TapeUp? It updates itself when you're not recording, or use Check for Updates… in the ··· menu.

item.title: TapeUp 0.1.4
item.description:
What's new

  • Remove only the audio. Once a recording has a transcript, a new button next to the trash removes its audio and keeps everything else. You can undo it right away. You can also right-click a recording to remove its audio.
  • Recordings without audio are marked. The card says "Transcript only", and lists show a small page icon before the length.
  • The trash button now says what it deletes: the whole recording, audio and transcript.

Install

Download TapeUp.dmg below and drag TapeUp to Applications, or:

brew install kkyrian/tap/tapeup

Already on TapeUp? It updates itself when you're not recording, or use Check for Updates… in the ··· menu.

item.title: TapeUp 0.1.3
item.description:
What's new

  • Speakers are labeled automatically. When a transcript is ready, TapeUp finds who spoke when, so you no longer need to click Label speakers. Imports still follow their Label speakers switch.
  • Your name comes first. When you say who was in a meeting or name a voice, your own name is the first suggestion. You set it on the People page. TapeUp doesn't add you on its own, so a meeting you missed won't list you.
  • Open at login is on for new installs. You can turn it off in Settings.
  • The floating timer stays on one line after the first hour.

Install

Download TapeUp.dmg below and drag TapeUp to Applications, or:

brew install kkyrian/tap/tapeup

Already on TapeUp? It updates itself when you're not recording, or use Check for Updates… in the ··· menu.

item.title: TapeUp 0.1.2
item.description:

  • The import bar moves while a long file copies. Before, it stayed at zero until the file was done.

Install

item.description:
What's new

  • The Get names from your AI button now opens the steps. It shows on a recording when TapeUp has no names to suggest yet. It now opens the People page at Fill from your AI: copy the request, paste it into your agent, then paste its answer back. Before, you had to find these steps yourself.

item.title: TapeUp 0.1.0
item.description:
The first release of TapeUp, a meeting recorder for Mac built for you and your AI agent.

What it does

  • Records any call. One click records your voice and everything your Mac plays, in any app. No bot joins the call. Press ⌥⌘R to start recording from any app, and small controls float over your windows to pause or stop.
  • Transcribes on your Mac while you talk, in 52 languages.
  • Finds who said what. Click Label speakers, and TapeUp finds each voice and shows a line it said. Play a voice to hear who it is.
  • Lists who was there. When you stop, tap how many people were on the call and type the first letters of each name.
  • Titles your recordings. Choose Claude Code or Codex in Settings, and it titles each recording and suggests who was there. It's off until you choose one. Without it, Apple Intelligence titles recordings on Macs that have it.
  • Imports old recordings from files or folders and transcribes them, with progress and the time left.
  • Finds any meeting by its title, the people in it, or anything that was said.
  • Works with your agent. Each recording is a folder of plain files with an AGENTS.md, and agents can use TapeUp's command line.
  • Keeps recording when AirPods connect or disconnect mid-call. Audio is saved as it records, so you keep the meeting even if TapeUp crashes.

Only the agent you choose sees a transcript.

Install

Download TapeUp.dmg below and drag TapeUp to Applications, or:

brew install kkyrian/tap/tapeup

TapeUp isn't notarized by Apple, so macOS stops it the first time. Click Done, then Open Anyway next to TapeUp in System Settings › Privacy & Security. It downloads its speech model once (2.3 GB, or 680 MB on Macs with less than 16 GB of memory).

Needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later; tested on macOS 27.

Updates

TapeUp checks once a day and installs updates when you're not recording. Turn that off under Settings › Automatic updates, or use Check for Updates… in the ··· menu.
